Though this appeal is listed for Admission, with the consent of the learned counsel for the parties,
the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. The claimants are in appeal dis-satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under the judgment and award, dated 03.01.2020, passed in M.V.C. No.1004/2018 by the V Additional District and Sessions Judge & Member, Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal') and praying for enhancement of compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The appellants/claimants - wife, children and mother of one Omkar Irannavar, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation for the accidental death of said Omkar Irannavar in a road traffic accident that took place on 21.05.2018, involving Maruti Ritz Car bearing registration No.MH-15/EP-9523.

They claimed that the NC:
2024:KHC-D:8043-DB deceased Omkar Irannavar was aged 26 years as on the date of the accident,
he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing cooking work in Vilas Hotel and an additional income of Rs.15,000/- by running a vada-pav & baji stall.

On issuance of notice, the respondent-insurance company filed its written statement denying the claim petition averments,
while admitting issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Maruti Ritz car in favour of respondent No.1.

Further, the insurer contended that the driver of the car had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident and also contended that the car was meant for personal use of the insured, but, on the date of the accident, it was plied to carry fare paid passengers.
Thus, it prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. On behalf of the claimants, claimant No.1 - the wife of the deceased - was examined as P.W.1 and two more witnesses were examined as P.Ws.2 and 3, apart from marking 24 documents as Exs.
P.1 to P.24
. No NC: 2024:KHC-D:8043-DB witness was examined nor was any document produced on behalf of the respondent.

The Tribunal, on scrutiny of the material on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.19,97,800/- with interest at 6% per annum on the following heads:
1 Loss of Dependency Rs. 19,27,800/- 2 Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/-

Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month, added 40% of the assessed income towards 'future prospects', adopted multiplier '17', and deducted 1/4th of the assessed income towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The claimants, not being satisfied with the above compensation awarded by the Tribunal, are before this Court praying for enhanced compensation.

5. Sri. Vitthal S.Teli, learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the Tribunal failed to properly NC: 2024:KHC-D:8043-DB assess the income of the deceased, and while assessing the notional income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month it committed a grave error.
Learned counsel further submits that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- by cooking work in the hotel and Rs.15,000/- by running on vada-pav and Bajji business in the evening hours.

Learned counsel would further submit that Ex.P.9, the certificate issued by Bhagyashree Co-operative Credit Society,
Shiraguppi, was placed on record to indicate that the deceased deposited more than Rs.95,000/- during the financial year 2014-15 as pigmy deposit.
Thus, learned counsel would submit that he had income of more than Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further, the learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal failed to award proper compensation under the head 'loss of consortium' in terms of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others1.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he prayed for allowing the appeal.

Per contra, Sri. Nagaraj C.Kolloori, learned counsel for the respondent No.2-insurance company would submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just compensation which needs no interference.

Further, the learned counsel submitted that in the absence of any material to establish the income, the Tribunal is justified in assessing the notional income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/-
per month.
Thus, he prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, and on perusal of the appeal papers, the points that fall for consideration in this appeal are,
i) Whether the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal is just and proper?
ii) Whether the claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation?

sentences.text: The answers to above points would be in the negative and affirmative respectively, for the following reasons.
(a) The accident that took place on 21.05.2018, involving Maruti Ritz Car bearing registration No.MH- 15/EP-9523 and the resultant death of Omkar Irannavar is not in dispute in this appeal.
The claimants are in this appeal praying for enhancement of compensation.
The insurer has not filed any appeal and has satisfied the award of the Tribunal.
(b) The accident is of the year 2018.
The income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.9,000/- per month is on the lower side.
The claimants have stated that the deceased was earning more than Rs.15,000/- by doing cooking work in hotel as well as by running vada-pav and Baji stall.
However, the claimants have not placed any material on record to establish the income and avocation of the deceased.
Ex. P.9
-certificate issued by Bhagyashree Co- operative Credit Society, is not proved in accordance with law, and no one is examined to prove the issuance of the certificate at Ex.P.9.
Therefore, the NC: 2024:KHC-D:8043-DB said document - Ex.P.9 cannot be taken note of while determining the income.
In the absence of any material to establish the income, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the year 2018 is Rs.11,750/- per month which is fixed taking note of various factors including the minimum wages.
Therefore, we re-assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.11,750/- per month.

The Tribunal, taking note of the age of the deceased as 26 years,
has rightly added 40% of the assessed income towards 'future prospects' and adopted appropriate multiplier '17', which needs no interference.
The Tribunal considering the number of dependants has rightly deducted 1/4th of the assessed income towards personal expenses of the deceased.

(c) Since the notional income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.11,750/-, the compensation, which - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8043-DB the claimants would be entitled to, under the head 'loss of dependency'
would be in a sum of Rs.25,16,850/- [Rs.11,750/- + Rs.4,700/- (40%) = Rs.16,450/- less Rs.4,112.50 (1/4th of Rs.16,450/-) = Rs.12,337.50 x 12 x 17].
(d) The Tribunal has erred in awarding a sum of Rs.40,000/- only towards 'loss of consortium'.

In terms of the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others2, and Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., (supra) the claimants,
being the wife, children and mother of the deceased, would be entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each on the head of 'loss of spousal, parental and filial consortium'.

9. The modified compensation under various heads is as follows:
1) Loss of Dependency Rs. 25,16,850/-
2) Loss of consortium (to claimants Rs. 1,76,000/-
 No.1 to 4) (Rs.40,000 x 4 + 10%)
 3) Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
 4) Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-
 TOTAL Rs. 27,25,850/-
Thus, the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.27,06,850/- as against Rs.19,97,800/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.27,25,850/- as against Rs.19,97,800/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8043-DB c) The enhanced compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

d) The respondent No.2-insurance company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made in the proportion as awarded by the Tribunal.
